objectives.title: Compare and contrast various types of security controls.

topics.label: Security control categories (technical, managerial, operational, physical)
Security control types (preventive, deterrent, detective, corrective, compensating, directive)

objectives.title: Summarize fundamental security concepts.

topics.label: Confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CIA) triad
Non-repudiation
Authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA)
Gap analysis
Zero Trust architecture (control plane vs data plane)
Physical security controls (bollards, vestibules, fencing, surveillance, guards, badges, lighting, sensors)
Deception and disruption technology (honeypots, honeynets, honeyfiles, honeytokens)

objectives.title: Explain the importance of change management processes and the impact to security.

topics.label: Change management business process (approval, ownership, stakeholders, impact analysis, test results, backout plan, maintenance window)
Change management technical implications (allow/deny lists, restricted activities, downtime, service and application restart, legacy applications, dependencies)
Change management documentation (diagrams, policies and procedures, version control, standard operating procedure)

objectives.title: Explain the importance of using appropriate cryptographic solutions.

topics.label: Public key infrastructure (public/private keys, key escrow)
Encryption levels (full-disk, partition, file, volume, database, record) and transport/communication
Cryptographic tools (TPM, HSM, key management system, secure enclave)
Obfuscation (steganography, tokenization, data masking)
Hashing
Salting
Digital signatures
Key stretching
Blockchain and open public ledgers
Certificates (CA, CRL, OCSP, self-signed, third-party, root of trust, CSR, wildcard)

objectives.title: Compare and contrast common threat actors and motivations.

topics.label: Threat actor types (nation-state, unskilled, hacktivist, insider, organized crime, shadow IT)
Threat actor attributes (internal/external, resources, sophistication)
Threat actor motivations (exfiltration, espionage, disruption, blackmail, financial gain, ideology, revenge, war)

objectives.title: Explain common threat vectors and attack surfaces.

topics.label: Message-based vectors (email, SMS, instant messaging)
Image-based vectors
File-based vectors
Voice call vectors
Removable device vectors
Unsecure networks (wireless, wired, Bluetooth) and open service ports
Default credentials as an attack surface
Supply chain vectors (MSPs, vendors, suppliers)
Human vectors and social engineering (phishing, vishing, smishing, misinformation/disinformation, impersonation, BEC, pretexting, watering hole, brand impersonation, typosquatting)

objectives.title: Explain various types of vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Application vulnerabilities (memory injection, buffer overflow, race conditions, TOCTOU, malicious update)
Operating system-based vulnerabilities
Web-based vulnerabilities (SQL injection, cross-site scripting)
Hardware vulnerabilities (firmware, end-of-life, legacy)
Virtualization vulnerabilities (VM escape, resource reuse)
Supply-chain and cloud-specific vulnerabilities (service, hardware, and software providers)
Cryptographic vulnerabilities
Misconfiguration vulnerabilities
Mobile device vulnerabilities (side loading, jailbreaking)
Zero-day vulnerabilities

objectives.title: Given a scenario, analyze indicators of malicious activity.

topics.label: Malware attacks (ransomware, trojan, worm, spyware, bloatware, virus, keylogger, logic bomb, rootkit)
Physical attacks (brute force, RFID cloning, environmental)
Network attacks (DDoS, DNS, wireless, on-path, credential replay, malicious code)
Application attacks (injection, buffer overflow, replay, privilege escalation, forgery, directory traversal)
Cryptographic attacks (downgrade, collision, birthday, amplified/reflected)
Password attacks (spraying, brute force)
Indicators of compromise (account lockout, concurrent sessions, blocked content, impossible travel, resource consumption, missing logs, out-of-cycle logging)

objectives.title: Explain the purpose of mitigation techniques used to secure the enterprise.

topics.label: Segmentation and isolation
Access control (ACLs, permissions) and least privilege
Application allow list
Patching and encryption
Hardening techniques (endpoint protection, host firewall, HIPS, disabling ports/protocols, default password changes, removing unnecessary software)
Monitoring
Decommissioning
Configuration enforcement

objectives.title: Compare and contrast security implications of different architecture models.

topics.label: Architecture and infrastructure concepts (cloud, on-premises, hybrid, third-party vendors, IaC, serverless, microservices, network infrastructure)
Virtualization and containerization
IoT, ICS/SCADA, embedded systems, and RTOS
Physical isolation (air gap) and logical segmentation (SDN)

Architecture considerations (availability, high availability, resilience, cost, responsiveness, scalability, ease of deployment, risk transference, ease of recovery, patch availability, inability to patch, power, compute)

objectives.title: Given a scenario, apply security principles to secure enterprise infrastructure.

topics.label: Infrastructure device placement and security zones (attack surface, connectivity, failure modes fail-open/fail-closed, active vs passive, inline vs tap)
Network appliances (jump server, proxy, IPS/IDS, load balancer, sensors, port security, 802.1X, EAP)
Firewall types (WAF, UTM, NGFW, layer 4/layer 7)
Secure communication and access (VPN, remote access, tunneling, TLS, IPSec, SD-WAN, SASE)
Selection of effective controls

objectives.title: Compare and contrast concepts and strategies to protect data.

topics.label: Data types (public, regulated, restricted, trade secret, private, intellectual property, legal, financial, human vs non-human readable)
Data classifications (sensitive, confidential)
Data states (at rest, in transit, in use) and data sovereignty/geolocation
Methods to secure data (geographic restrictions, encryption, hashing, masking, tokenization, obfuscation, segmentation, permission restrictions)
Data loss prevention (DLP)

objectives.title: Explain the importance of resilience and recovery in security architecture.

topics.label: High availability (load balancing vs clustering)
Site considerations (hot, cold, warm, geographic dispersion)
Platform diversity and multi-cloud systems
Continuity of operations and capacity planning (people, technology, infrastructure)
Backups (onsite/offsite, frequency, encryption, snapshots) and replication
Journaling
Power resilience (generators, UPS)
Resilience testing (tabletop exercises, failover, simulation, parallel processing)
Recovery metrics (RTO, RPO, MTTR, MTBF)

objectives.title: Given a scenario, apply common security techniques to computing resources.

topics.label: Secure baselines (establish, deploy, maintain)
Hardening targets (mobile devices, workstations, switches, routers, cloud infrastructure, servers, ICS/SCADA, embedded, RTOS, IoT)
Mobile solutions (MDM, deployment models BYOD/COPE/CYOD, connection methods cellular/Wi-Fi/Bluetooth)
Wireless security settings (WPA3, AAA/RADIUS, cryptographic and authentication protocols)
Application security (input validation, secure cookies, static code analysis, code signing)
Sandboxing
Monitoring of computing resources
Wireless installation considerations (site surveys, heat maps)

objectives.title: Explain the security implications of proper hardware, software, and data asset management.

topics.label: Acquisition and procurement process
Assignment and accounting (ownership, classification)
Monitoring and asset tracking (inventory)
Disposal and decommissioning (sanitization, destruction, certification, data retention)
Asset enumeration

objectives.title: Explain various activities associated with vulnerability management.

topics.label: Vulnerability identification methods (vulnerability scan, application security static/dynamic analysis, package monitoring, threat feed, OSINT, proprietary/third-party, ISAC, dark web, penetration testing, responsible disclosure, bug bounty, system/process audit)

Vulnerability analysis (confirmation, false positive, false negative, prioritization, CVSS, CVE, vulnerability classification, exposure factor, environmental variables, industry impact, risk tolerance)
Vulnerability response, remediation, and validation (patching, insurance, segmentation, compensating controls, exceptions and exemptions, rescanning, audit, verification)
Vulnerability reporting

objectives.title: Explain security alerting and monitoring concepts and tools.

topics.label: Monitoring computing resources (systems, applications, infrastructure)
Monitoring activities (log aggregation, alerting, scanning, reporting, archiving)
Alert response, remediation, and validation (quarantine, alert tuning)
Monitoring tools (SCAP, benchmarks, agents/agentless, SIEM, antivirus, DLP, SNMP traps, NetFlow, vulnerability scanners)

objectives.title: Given a scenario, modify enterprise capabilities to enhance security.

topics.label: Firewall hardening (rules, access lists, ports/protocols, screened subnets)
IDS/IPS tuning (trends, signatures)
Web filtering (agent-based, centralized proxy, URL scanning, content categorization, block rules, reputation)
Operating system security (Group Policy, SELinux)
Implementation of secure protocols (protocol selection, port selection, transport method)
DNS filtering and email security (DMARC, DKIM, SPF)
File integrity monitoring
Data loss prevention
Network access control (NAC)
Endpoint detection and response (EDR), extended detection and response (XDR), and user behavior analytics

objectives.title: Given a scenario, implement and maintain identity and access management.

topics.label: Provisioning and de-provisioning user accounts
Permission assignments and implications (DAC, RBAC, rule-based, ABAC, time-of-day restrictions, least privilege)
Identity proofing
Federation, SSO, and interoperability (LDAP, OAuth, SAML)
Attestation
Multifactor authentication (biometrics, hard/soft tokens, security keys, factors)
Password concepts (best practices, length, complexity, reuse, expiration, age, password managers) and passwordless
Privileged access management (just-in-time permissions, password vaulting, ephemeral credentials)

objectives.title: Explain the importance of automation and orchestration related to secure operations.

topics.label: Automation and scripting use cases (user/resource provisioning, guard rails, security groups, ticket creation, escalation, enabling/disabling services and access)
Automation benefits (efficiency, enforcing baselines, standard configurations, scaling, employee retention, reaction time, workforce multiplier, CI/testing)
Automation cautions (complexity, cost, single point of failure, technical debt, ongoing supportability, API integrations)

objectives.title: Explain appropriate incident response activities.

topics.label: Incident response process and training (preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned, tabletop exercises, simulation)
Root cause analysis and threat hunting
Digital forensics (legal hold, chain of custody, acquisition, reporting, preservation, e-discovery)

objectives.title: Given a scenario, use data sources to support an investigation.

topics.label: Log data (firewall, application, endpoint, OS-specific security, IPS/IDS, network logs)
Investigation data sources (vulnerability scans, automated reports, dashboards, packet captures, metadata)

objectives.title: Summarize elements of effective security governance.

topics.label: Security governance documents (guidelines, policies, standards, procedures)
Policy types (AUP, information security, business continuity, disaster recovery, incident response, SDLC, change management)
Roles and responsibilities (owners, controllers, processors, custodians/stewards)
Governance structures (boards, committees, government entities, centralized/decentralized)
Monitoring and revision of governance
External considerations (regulatory, legal, industry, local/regional, national, global)

objectives.title: Explain elements of the risk management process.

topics.label: Risk identification and risk register
Risk assessment (ad hoc, recurring, one-time, continuous)
Risk analysis (qualitative, quantitative, SLE, ALE, ARO, probability, likelihood, exposure factor)
Risk tolerance, risk appetite (expansionary, conservative, neutral), and risk threshold
Risk management strategies (transfer, accept, exemption, exception, avoid, mitigate)
Risk reporting and key risk indicators
Business impact analysis (RTO, RPO, MTTR, MTBF)

objectives.title: Explain the processes associated with third-party risk assessment and management.

topics.label: Vendor assessment (penetration testing, right-to-audit clause, evidence of internal audits, independent assessments, supply chain analysis)
Vendor selection (due diligence, conflict of interest)
Agreement types (SLA, MOA, MOU, MSA, WO/SOW, NDA, BPA)
Vendor monitoring, questionnaires, and rules of engagement

objectives.title: Summarize elements of effective security compliance.

topics.label: Compliance reporting (internal, external) and consequences of non-compliance (fines, sanctions, reputational damage, loss of license, contractual impacts)
Compliance monitoring (due diligence/care, attestation and acknowledgement, internal and external, automation)
Privacy (legal implications, local/regional/national/global, data subject, controller vs processor, ownership, data inventory and retention, right to be forgotten)
Key regulations (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, FERPA, GLBA)

objectives.title: Explain types and purposes of audits and assessments.

topics.label: Audits (internal, external, audit committee, self-assessments, regulatory, examinations, independent third-party)
Attestation
Penetration testing (offensive, defensive, integrated, known/partially known/unknown environment, reconnaissance, passive/active)

objectives.title: Given a scenario, implement security awareness practices.

topics.label: Phishing (campaigns, recognizing attempts, responding to reported messages)
Anomalous behavior recognition (risky, unexpected, unintentional) and insider threat
User guidance and training (policy/handbooks, situational awareness, hybrid/remote work environments)

Social engineering awareness and operational security
Reporting and monitoring (initial, recurring) and program development/execution
